selected.name: MQTT_UAD (MQTT Under Attack Dataset)
selected.authors: Aveleira-Mata, Alaiz-Moretón, Bayón-Gutiérrez, García-Ordás, Prieto-Fernández, García-Rodríguez et al.
selected.licence: CC BY 4.0 (attribution required; redistribution permitted with credit)
selected.granularity: one row per captured network frame, 67 features per frame (per the paper's abstract)
selected.intended_use: Training and testing ML-based intrusion detection for MQTT networks in home and industrial settings

verified_from_public_pages: Title, authors, 2025 publication, figshare DOI and CC BY 4.0 licence
Three CSV files: DoS, MitM and Intrusion, with the frame counts listed above
67 features per frame, labelled normal and attack traffic captured on a real MQTT testbed in Spain
NOT_verified: Exact column names and the label-column encoding (the paper could not be opened in the build environment)
A stable direct-download URL: download manually from the DOI page; the notebook then validates the schema
What the 'Intrusion' attack consists of beyond its name

alternatives_considered.name: MQTTEEB-D
alternatives_considered.note: Real MySignals/Raspberry Pi testbed with several processed variants. Licence not verified; a good second dataset.

alternatives_considered.name: MQTT-IoT-IDS2020
alternatives_considered.note: Simulated MQTT network with flow-based features and an open-access licence. Simulated testbed.

alternatives_considered.name: BCCC-IoT-MQTT-IDS-2025
alternatives_considered.note: Large combination of three MQTT datasets (millions of records). Too big for a semester demo.

why_selected: Small enough to train in a free Colab runtime, openly licensed, frame-level labelled CSVs, and real captured MQTT traffic.
known_limitations: Each file mixes normal and attack traffic of one attack family; normal traffic is therefore captured in different sessions per file, so a model can partly learn the capture session rather than the attack.
Frames are not independent; a random row split would leak. The notebook uses contiguous-block splitting.

The poster's kill chain (credential brute force, wildcard topic enumeration) is not guaranteed to be represented in this dataset. The simulator covers those scenarios with rules; the ML model is not evaluated on them.
Class imbalance is strong in MitM and Intrusion files.
